questions.question: The build's rules retry is skipped once 80 s have passed, and in the canonical Waltzman build the test run starts at 85-111 s. Should the cut-off, or the order of the build steps, change so the retry can repair a world?
questions.blocks: whether a world whose rules fail the part-way or liveness checks can be repaired on the live path, or only scored lower
questions.resolves_with: An argument already settles that the retry is skipped (85, 101 and 111 s against 80 s). In those runs the test run found no part-way problem, so nothing needed repair (c1r24 TRACE_READ.md:54): it is a latent risk for a world that does. What is left is a technical trade-off against the 150 s first-round target: measure where the build's time goes in the saved build traces (free) and either start the test run earlier or tie the cut-off to the time left before that target.

questions.short: A refusal is not linked to its cause
questions.question: When several people want the one shared thing in a round, each loser is told 'your choice was no longer allowed after earlier moves this round; choose again' and is shown the round's earlier moves (who, which rule), so it can see who moved. It is not told which of its moves was refused or which earlier move blocked it, and the record does not link the refusal to that move. Should the retry prompt and the row name the refused move and the blocking event?
questions.blocks: whether a reader of a run (or the readout) can say why a person's move was refused, in any world
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles it: the run loop already knows which submitted event changed the revision before the loser's pick, so naming it costs nothing and belongs in the run loop, not any world. Build it and check on free replays of saved worlds (c1r24 Waltzman, truck) that each refused row names its blocking event id. Starting point: c1r24 call 18016 shows the round's moves but not the link.

questions.question: People put the decision on the agenda and settle it again for 25 rounds (c1r24 r22-r46). Is that because group_decision.agenda_items is a bare count, so an item says nothing, or because put-matter-on-agenda and settle-agenda-matter are offered every work cycle at no cost?
questions.blocks: whether the group-decision family's agenda needs content or should be dropped
questions.resolves_with: An argument makes the content cause likely (the partnership said at c1r24 round 40 it should not add an item 'when I lack information'), but the residents' behaviour cannot be shown on a free replay, which uses scripted moves with no AI. It needs one paid owner-allowance run, and only once Q12 or a goal makes the agenda matter: the result decides whether to give items content, cost them, or drop the count. A free replay can only check that items carry content.

questions.short: Notice only as good as the words
questions.question: A finished-task notice repeats the starter's own words about the work, and vague words ('address the retention period') leave the others unable to see what was decided. Should a concern's remedy record a structured answer instead?
questions.blocks: whether E2 (a fix carries its substance) holds for every world or only when residents happen to write specific words
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles that the notice cannot be more specific than its source words (c1r24 round 10). The decision is technical: require the remedy's work answer to say yes or no to the concern's question plus what was set, then check it on one free replay.

questions.question: People say 'deployed but not authorized' while the decision is deployed. Is this a state label the residents are shown, or the model misreading correct state?
questions.blocks: whether to change how state is shown to residents or leave it as model error
questions.resolves_with: One counterexample settles it: open the resident prompt of one such round (c1r24 round 15, logistics) and read what the status field said.
questions.evidence: A label the residents are shown. Logistics' call 18032 (c1r24) shows the decision as 'status deployed, support 5' (correct) and its own member record as 'approved False, authorized False': two fields every person gets and no rule ever writes (compile_spec.py:33-34, set at :626). Filed as #231.

questions.question: The page sent one round's /run twice and the server ran and billed both (#225). Should /run refuse a second request for the same round?
questions.blocks: wasted spend and shares that keep only one of two runs
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles it: a /run keyed by session, round and base revision is safe to refuse twice whatever sent the duplicate. Build it with a test that sends the same round twice.

questions.question: Each long build call is sent twice; does the losing copy still run to the end (#226)?
questions.blocks: about $0.03 per build and misleading calls in the build trace
questions.resolves_with: Reading the code settles it.
questions.evidence: Yes. hedged() returns the first good copy and never stops the other (people_world.py:195-212); _settle_late_hedges only reserves budget for it and charges its cost when it ends (world_builder_service.py:266-285). Whether to cancel it stays with #226.

questions.short: Rules check a resource but never claim it
questions.question: Generated rules can check a shared resource without ever using it up, so the finish line passes while the constraint is lost (#218). Can the build catch that?
questions.blocks: whether a finished build is faithful to what was described
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles that it is decidable: a field read by a check but never written by any rule is a static finding. Add it to the test-run findings and check the saved worlds.

questions.short: Test run too short for some tasks
questions.question: The 12-round scripted test run rejects correct rules for task worlds that need more rounds (#217). Should it run longer?
questions.blocks: builds wrongly scored as failing and the rewrite spend they cause
questions.resolves_with: One counterexample already exists (the garden world finishes at round 15). Lengthen the free test run for task worlds and check the saved fixtures still score the same.

questions.question: After a lost race the retry's own words are stored as said_on_retry, but the 'What happened' readout quotes only said, the words behind the first choice, next to the move the retry made. Should the readout quote the retry's words?
questions.blocks: whether the readout's quoted words match the move that ran
questions.resolves_with: Reading the code settles it: the row keeps both (run_authored_world.py:584, :599-600) and the scene replay already prefers said_on_retry (render_scene_replay.py:398), but run_readout.py:93 reads said only. Make the readout prefer said_on_retry the same way and check it on a free replay.

questions.question: Is a recipient's resident memory still seeded with information before the information is delivered (#212 item 3)?
questions.blocks: whether beliefs can run ahead of what the world has shown a person
questions.resolves_with: One counterexample settles it: read the round-1 prompts of run c1r24 (calls 17868-17878) for a recipient that mentions its concern before delivery.
questions.evidence: No. In c1r24 round 1 the four countries that receive concerns see none of them (calls 17868, 17870, 17876, 17877-17878: 'sees: none'); each group sees only its own (leakcheck.txt, leaks 0). The concerns were delivered later in round 1 (r1-e00001, r1-e00011, r1-e00013, r1-e00019).

questions.question: A people-world run ends at the round cap even when nothing has changed for 20 rounds. Should it stop when the decision is settled and nothing changes?
questions.blocks: how long visitors watch a run, and its cost
questions.resolves_with: This is a product call on what a finished story looks like; no test settles it.
questions.recommendation: Stop a people-world run when the decision is deployed or rejected and no person's move has changed anything for one full operating-review period (6 rounds, compile_spec.py:442), and say so on the page.
questions.default: Runs keep ending at the round cap the visitor picked.

questions.question: The roadmap's hardening queue (executable-law fingerprint, role-specific write scopes, explicit move-cap overflow) and the run-loop fixes above (Q2, Q6) compete for the next goal. Which comes first?
questions.blocks: the next goal
questions.resolves_with: A priority call; the argument for the run-loop fixes is that they affect every world on every run today.
questions.recommendation: Do the run-loop fixes first (Q6 no double run, Q10 readout words, Q2 refusal linked to its cause), then the executable-law fingerprint.
questions.default: The next goal is the run-loop fixes (docs/plans/run-loop-contention.goal.md).

questions.question: Decision 008 says worlds are built in an agent harness that drafts, checks and edits, but the live service does not call scripts/world_harness.py. Is the harness to be wired into the live build?
questions.blocks: whether build repairs come from a harness or from the rules retry (Q1)
questions.resolves_with: Reading the code and the decision settles the current state (not imported by the service; the decision says it has not been shown on the live server). What it would take is a build-time measurement against the 150 s target, from saved build traces first.

questions.question: The ~/code2 repository format check fails: no docs/index.md, docs/architecture/arc42.md, C4 files, openspec specs, lefthook.yml or Makefile. Should world-substrate adopt the format?
questions.blocks: whether the repo-format check passes
questions.resolves_with: Prior art settles the shape (phenomenal-meaning adopted it); the work is mechanical: add the files, mostly as indexes over the existing architecture, ODD and trace documents.

questions.question: This repository's work ran as /goal documents, which never pass plan adoption, so nothing required a planning package. Should writing a goal require one?
questions.blocks: whether the next goal can again run without a current system model and question list
questions.resolves_with: An argument: Brian approved on 2026-10-21 that every plan carries a planning package, and a goal is a plan. But a hard check would refuse new goals in every repository that has no package yet, so how strictly to enforce it is a priority call.
questions.recommendation: Make the goal validator (agent-skills, skills/authoring-goals/scripts/validate_goal_authority.py) refuse a goal document without a 'Planning package:' line or a named exemption, so goal-driven repositories meet the same gate as adopted plans.
questions.default: The goal-writing skill only tells authors to name the package; nothing refuses a goal without one. This repository's next goal already names its package.

questions.question: The offline any-scenario pipeline has no view of its model and checks (G13) and no approval step (G14). Should it get them, or stay an offline spike?
questions.blocks: whether work goes into the offline pipeline at all
questions.resolves_with: A scope call; the live path now builds people worlds itself, so the pipeline matters less.
questions.recommendation: Keep it an offline spike: no views or approval step, since the live World Builder is where people build worlds.
questions.default: No work on G13 or G14.

questions.question: When a resident tries something no installed rule covers, may an AI game master invent a rough effect, marked coarse in the record?
questions.blocks: slice S4 of docs/plans/open_attempt.md, and how alive a world feels when its rules are thin
questions.resolves_with: A product call on whether every effect must come from a written rule; no test settles it.
